newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia stocks trend up on year-end buying and Dow.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks trend up on year-end buying and Dow.

text.p: Most Asian stock markets achieved modest gains on Friday as light year-end buying and the strength of U.S. stocks got the better of any niggling bearish tendencies.
Tokyo climbed 0.40 percent and Hong Kong 0.47 percent, but Seoul was a notable exception and shed 1.18 percent as the market remained blighted by the current wave of industrial action.

Tokyo stocks clawed higher by the end of trade after a day in which indices seesawed, lifted by bargain-hunting and depressed by profit-taking, brokers said. They said most investors were wary after the Nikkei average plunged below the 19,000 threshold on Thursday.
The Nikkei 225 settled 77.46 points or 0.40 percent higher at 19,369.04.
"Some shares that were looking a bit oversold rebounded and buying of global issues, especially by pension funds, helped the Nikkei average end on a firm tone," one analyst said.
Hong Kong stocks closed up, buoyed by the outlook for the local property market and positive trends on Wall Street, brokers said.
"Hongkong Bank's comments on the property market were reassuring and helped (market) sentiment," said James Osborn in institutional sales at ING Barings.
HSBC Holdings general manager Christopher Langley said that Hongkong Bank did not see any sign of a speculative bubble in the medium priced residential property market.
The Hang Seng Index closed 62.53 points higher at 13,404.14, after moving to a day high of 13,451.16 in the early trade. Turnover was HK$5.65 billion.
Seoul stocks closed sharply lower on the last trading day of 1996 as spreading labour unrest dampened already weak investor sentiment, brokers said.
The composite index provisionally ended at 651.22, the lowest closing level this year. This was down 7.79 points or 1.18 percent on the day.
Brokers said a deteriorating labour situation, sparked by Thursday's passage of a new labour law, remained the biggest single factor dampening the market.
Thai stocks bounced 1.12 percent as late bargain-hunting helped wipe out earlier losses made on lingering concern about weak economic indicators, brokers said.
The SET index advanced 9.23 points to 835.71 on thin 2.2 billion baht turnover.
Singapore shares crept up on low volumes with dealers in search of something to kick start the market and lift activity ahead of the new year.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended up 4.91 points at 2,202.60.
Kuala Lumpur's blue chip focused Composite Index ended up 1.32 points to 1,209.00 in light holiday business, while Taiwan's weighted index slid 26.01 points or 0.38 percent to end at 6,863.02 .
Manila closed 5.04 points, or 0.16 percent, up at 3,170.56 as late buying for window-dressing lifted stocks. traders said.
Late session window-dressing also pushed Jakarta share prices higher, with the composite index up 4.94 points, or 0.78 percent, at 637.43 points by the close.
New Zealand's top 40 index ended 5.72 up at 2350.42, while the All Ordinaries in Australia ended 14.2 points up at 2,395.6.
February Brent on Simex was quoted at $23.50 a barrel, up 11 cents on the London settlement price on Tuesday.

The dollar was hovering close to 115 yen in slack late Tokyo business. At 1042 GMT, the dollar traded at 115.02/12 yen and 1.5538/45 marks, against respective New York closes at 114.88/98 yen and 1.5528/38 marks.
Hong Kong gold bullion ended at US$369.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$368.60/369.10 close on Thursday.
